titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 15, the hymns (part 2 of 4)
part: Spell 15 — the hymns, part 2 of 4: a litany of greetings to Osiris and a hymn to Ra at his rising in the eastern horizon (Plates 19–20)
about: The second part of Spell 15 begins on Plate 19 with a litany: ten short strophes, the first nine opening with the greeting 'hail to you' written in red, that hail Osiris by his names and his cities (Heliopolis, Busiris, Heracleopolis, Abydos, Nekhen) and end with Ani asking for a way to pass in peace. On Plate 20 a new hymn begins, to Ra as he rises in the eastern horizon: Ani asks that his ba may travel with the sun in its two barks, and then greets the sun as Horakhty and Khepri, the god whom those in the Duat come out to see. It ends as Ani says he has come to the land of eternity, and the hymn runs on into the next part. Budge's type is uncertain in several signs, and the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · the-stars · in · Heliopolis(?) · the-Henmemet · in · Kher-aha(?)
sentences.i: Hail to you, (you of) the stars in Heliopolis(?) and of the Henmemet in Kher-aha(?)!
sentences.n: The litany of Spell 15 begins: ten strophes, the first nine opening with ind ḥr·k 'hail to you', which the papyrus writes in red (Budge's line numerals 1 to 10 mark them, one line to a strophe). ind is the reed i and a post with a knobbed top (the sign nḏ, Aa27, approximate), here without the papyrus roll; ḥr·k is the face ḥr with its stroke and the basket ·k: literally 'greetings to your face', as in the first part of the spell. Budge prints ànet' and ḥrà-k as two groups, and they stay two words. ḫꜣbsw 'stars' is a sign coded M12, the lotus ḫꜣ (in the print a stalk with a curled top on a flared base, approximate; Q7 does not fit; M12 writes ḫꜣ in Spell 1 as well), read ḫꜣ with Budge, ꜣ as complement, foot b, the folded cloth s, the star as classifier and plural strokes; the reading of the first sign is doubtful. m iwnw: the pillar iwn stands alone (O28, approximate), perhaps a short writing of iwnw 'Heliopolis', which is spelled in full at the end of the strophe; Budge leaves it as Àn. ḥnmmt 'the Henmemet' is the disk with hanging rays (N8), the owl m twice, t and plural strokes: beings of the sun's light. ḫr-ꜥḥꜣ is the butcher's block ḫr (T28, approximate), a rounded stela (O26, approximate), a low sign with marks (N29, approximate) and the town sign; Budge reads χer-āba. It is taken, doubtfully, as Kher-aha, the district by Heliopolis named in Spell 125 (written there ḫ-r-ꜥ-ḥ-ꜣ); here only ḫr and the town sign are clear: neither the stela nor the low sign has a value that spells ꜥḥꜣ, and the stela is coded as carrying it only because the reading needs a place for it. No 'lord of' is written: Budge supplies '[lord of] … [and of]'; the vocative is kept as it stands, and the English supplies only '(you of)' to make the relation readable.

sentences.l: Wenty · more-effective · than · the-gods · hidden · who-are-in(?) · Heliopolis
sentences.i: Wenty, more effective than the hidden gods who are in(?) Heliopolis!
sentences.n: wnty 'Wenty' (Budge: Unti) is the hare wn with water n as complement, t, two strokes y and the seated god: a god's name, perhaps 'he who exists' from wnn 'be'. Budge supplies '[thou]'. ꜣḫ r nṯrw 'more effective than the gods': the adjective ꜣḫ 'effective, glorious' (Budge: 'glorious more') (the crested ibis ꜣḫ, ḫ as complement; the chick w after it, Budge's χu, is not read, then a tall sign with ticks, Y1a, and a stroke) followed by r 'than', the way Egyptian makes a comparison. nṯrw is the flag written three times. štꜣ 'hidden' is the long hatched rectangle š (N37, approximate), a flat sign with grains taken as tꜣ (N16, approximate), a small cup (W10, approximate; taken as a classifier) and ꜣ, with the crossed sticks and a flat sign with a tuft (Aa13, approximate) as classifiers: the adjective after nṯrw, its plural ending unwritten. imyt is Z11 im with m and t: the nisba 'who is in', but feminine where 'the gods' would want imyw; it may be the preposition imytw 'among' (Budge: àmt, as in the first part of the spell), and the form is doubtful. iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the pillar, the pot nw and the town sign.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · Pillar · in · Iun-des(?) · Horus · in · the-two-horizons · wide · of-stride · crosses · he · the-sky
sentences.i: Hail to you, Pillar in Iun-des(?), Horus in the two horizons, wide of stride as he crosses the sky!
sentences.n: Strophe 2; ind ḥr·k in red as before. iwn 'Pillar' is the pillar (O28, approximate) with a stroke, three small strokes and the seated god: a name of the god, as in the hymn to Osiris (Budge: Àn). iwn-ds is the pillar again with a knife lying across (coded T30, read ds with Budge, approximate) over a low sign with a wavy top (N25, approximate); Budge reads Àn-ṭes with a (?) in his English, and the place is not known. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon with r and the seated god. ꜣḫty 'the two horizons' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ, t, two strokes y and two dotted oblongs as classifiers (N18, approximate; no horizon sign N27 is printed): the dual of ꜣḫt, the horizons of sunrise and sunset. pd nmtt 'wide of stride': p, a bar with turned-down ends (coded N1, approximate; perhaps the bow pḏ, which writes this word elsewhere in the papyrus), the hand d and the walking legs, then nmtt 'stride', the legs with t and a stroke; Budge prints peṭ and nemmat, and the legs after the hand are taken with pd. ḏꜣ·f ḥrt 'he crosses the sky': ḏꜣ is a tall tapering sign (the fire-drill ḏꜣ, U28, approximate) with ꜣ and a boat as classifier (P1, approximate), a sḏm·f with ·f; ḥrt is the face, r, t and the sky. The god is the sun striding across heaven.

morph.gloss: horizon (noun f.); dual ꜣḫty 'the two horizons', of sunrise and sunset

sentences.l: he · Horakhty
sentences.i: He is Horakhty.
sentences.n: ntf ḥr-ꜣḫty 'he is Horakhty': ntf, the independent pronoun 'he' (water n, t, the horned viper f), with a noun after it makes a sentence with no verb, 'he is N'. ḥr-ꜣḫty 'Horakhty', 'Horus of the horizon', is the falcon ḥr and the horizon sign ꜣḫt (the sun between two hills, N27) with t and two strokes y, then two hollow oblongs as classifiers (coded N18, approximate; undotted here); Budge prints it as one group, Ḥeru-χuti. Most of the strophes end with such a sentence naming the god.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · ba · this · of · eternity · the-ba · who-is-in · Busiris · Wennefer · son · of-Nut
sentences.i: Hail to you, this ba of eternity, the ba who is in Busiris, Wennefer, son of Nut!
sentences.n: Strophe 3; ind ḥr·k in red. bꜣ 'ba' is the ram (E10), the ba-sign of the ram of Mendes, with a small incense bowl before it (R7, the house practice) and a stroke. pw 'this' (p and the chick w) is the demonstrative after its noun; n ḥḥ 'of eternity' is the genitive n and the wick ḥ twice with the sun-disk between as classifier, the n of nḥḥ unwritten as in the first part of the spell. The second bꜣ is the ram with its stroke, two reeds and the seated god (Budge: Bai, 'Ram-god'); the two reeds are not read, and may make the word bꜣy. imy ḏdw 'who is in Busiris': imy is Z11 im with m and two strokes y; ḏdw 'Busiris' (Djedu) is the djed-pillar twice, w and the town sign. wnn-nfr 'Wennefer', 'he who is (always) perfect', is the hare wn with water twice, the heart-and-windpipe nfr and the seated god. sꜣ nwt 'son of Nut': the pintail duck sꜣ with its stroke, and nwt written with the pot nw, t and the sky, with a cobra on a basket (I13, approximate) as classifier. The ba of Osiris was held to rest in Busiris, his city in the Delta.

sentences.l: he · lord · of-Igeret
sentences.i: He is the lord of Igeret.
sentences.n: ntf nb igrt 'he is the lord of Igeret': ntf 'he' with the noun phrase after it, as in strophe 2. nb 'lord' is the basket nb; igrt 'Igeret' is the reed i, the jar-stand g, r and t, with a low sign with a wavy top (N25, approximate) for the hill country: the realm of the dead, perhaps 'the silent land' (Budge: Àḳert).

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · in · ruling · your · Busiris
sentences.i: Hail to you in your rule over Busiris!
sentences.n: Strophe 4; ind ḥr·k in red. m ḥqꜣ·k ḏdw: after m 'in', ḥqꜣ 'rule' is the infinitive, with ·k as its subject and ḏdw as its object, 'in your ruling Busiris'. ḥqꜣ is the crook with a small triangle q as complement (N29, approximate) over a flat sign with a tuft (Aa13, approximate), a classifier here, and the basket ·k. ḏdw 'Busiris' is written this time with one djed-pillar, the hand d as complement, w and the town sign.

sentences.l: the-Great-Crown · established · on · head · your
sentences.i: The Great Crown stands firm on your head.
sentences.n: wrrt 'the Great Crown' is the swallow wr with r and t, and as classifier a crown with a curl set on a basket (coded S4, the red crown on a basket, approximate; the shape is unclear); one r is written where the word has two (Budge: urert). mn 'established' is the gaming board mn with n and the papyrus roll: the stative after its subject, ending unwritten. m 'on' is the flat sign Aa15; tp·k 'your head' is the head in profile with its stroke and ·k. The crown is the sign of Osiris' kingship.

sentences.l: you · the-One · who-makes · protection · his · rest · you · in · Busiris
sentences.i: You are the One who makes his own protection; you rest in Busiris.
sentences.n: ntk wꜥ 'you are the One': ntk 'you' (n, t, the basket k) with a noun after it, the 2nd-person form of ntf. wꜥ 'one' is the harpoon with its stroke, and U15 standing where the arm ꜥ is read as complement (as often in this copy; Budge reads ā). ir mkt·f 'who makes his protection': ir is the eye alone, the participle of iri 'do, make'; mkt 'protection' is the owl m with an arm joined to it (G17 with D36, a ligature; the arm is not read), the basket k, t, a flat sign with a tuft (Aa13, approximate) and a stroke as classifiers, and ·f, which looks back to the One himself (Budge: māket-f, 'his strength'). ḥtp·k m ḏdw 'you rest in Busiris': the offering table ḥtp with ·k, a sḏm·f.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · as · lord · of-the-Naret-tree · setting · the-Sokar-bark · upon · sledge(?) · its
sentences.i: Hail to you as lord of the Naret-tree, setting the Sokar-bark upon its sledge(?),
sentences.n: Strophe 5; ind ḥr·k in red. m nb nꜥrt 'as lord of the Naret-tree': nꜥrt is water n, U15 for ꜥ, r and t, with a tree crossed by a line ending in a point (coded M1, approximate) and the seated god as classifiers (Budge: Nārt, 'the acacia-tree'): the sacred tree of Heracleopolis, the city named in strophe 6. rdit 'setting, placing' is the infinitive of rdi: r over t, and the low flat sign U15 standing where the giving arm di is written, as the same sign stands for the arm ꜥ throughout this copy (Budge: erṭāt). skr is the bolt s, the basket k and r, with a small cross (Z9) and a bark on a sledge carrying a falcon (coded P3, approximate) as classifiers: Sokar, here his bark, as in Spell 1, 'placing the Henu-bark of Sokar upon its sledge(?)'. ḥr 'upon' is the face with its stroke. tmt·f is t, the sledge tm (U15) with m, t, a curved line ending in a point (coded V1, approximate) as classifier and ·f; Budge reads temt-f, 'its sledge', and the word is doubtful. The bark of Sokar was drawn round the walls of Memphis on its sledge at his feast.

sentences.l: who-repels · the-Rebel · the-doer · of-evil · who-lets · rest · the-wedjat · at · place · its
sentences.i: who repels the Rebel, the doer of evil, who lets the wedjat rest in its place.
sentences.n: ḫsf 'who repels' is the spindle crossed by the viper (the ligature ḫsf, U35, approximate) with U15 as classifier, the participle of ḫsf 'oppose, repel' (Budge prints 'esef' small). sbiw 'the Rebel' is s, b, the reed, w, a small ring (N33, approximate) and the forked post (Aa26, approximate) as classifiers: the serpent enemy of the sun (Budge: Sebàu). ir ḏw 'doer of evil': the participle ir with ḏw 'evil', the mountain ḏw with the curl w as complement and the bird of bad things. di ḥtp wḏꜣt 'who lets the wedjat rest': di, the participle of rdi, is the giving arm with a loaf (D37, approximate), with a sḏm·f after it, 'causes that it rest'; ḥtp is the offering table alone; wḏꜣt is the eye with the falcon's cheek-markings (D10) alone, the Sound Eye of Horus. r st·s 'at its place': st 'seat, place' is the seat (Q1) with t, a house-like sign (O1, approximate) and the bolt ·s 'its' (Budge prints àuset-s as one group). Restoring the Eye to its place is the work of Thoth and of the gods of order.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · strong · in · moment · his · great-one · mighty · foremost · of-Nairedef(?) · lord · of-eternity · maker · of-everlastingness
sentences.i: Hail to you, strong in his moment, great and mighty one, foremost of Nairedef(?), lord of eternity, maker of everlastingness!
sentences.n: Strophe 6; ind ḥr·k in red. wsr 'strong' is the head and neck of a jackal wsr with s and r as complements and U15 as classifier. m ꜣt·f 'in his moment': ꜣt 'moment, instant' is ꜣ and t, an animal head with open jaws (the leopard head ꜣt, F9, approximate), t again and the sun as classifier of time, with ·f; the god is strong at the moment he strikes. wr 'great one' is the swallow wr with r and a standing dignitary with a staff (A21) as classifier; ꜥꜣ 'mighty' is the column ꜥꜣ (O29, approximate) with U15 for the complement ꜥ and a flat sign with a tuft (Aa13, approximate). ḫnty 'foremost of' is the rack of jars ḫnt (W17, approximate), its ending unwritten. The name after it is water n, ꜣ, the reed, r, the hand d, a looped sign with splayed legs (coded T12, approximate), a house-like sign (O1, approximate) and f; Budge reads Na-àreṭ-f. It is the name of a place by Heracleopolis; read from the signs as n-ꜣird-f, its form and meaning are doubtful. nb ḥḥ ir ḏt 'lord of eternity, maker of everlastingness': ir is the participle of iri; ḏt is the cobra ḏ, t and a flat strip with grains (N16, approximate).

sentences.l: you · lord · of-Heracleopolis
sentences.i: You are the lord of Heracleopolis.
sentences.n: nn-nswt 'Heracleopolis' (Nen-nesut) is written with the sedge nsw, t and n first, then a seated figure with a hand at the face (A1, approximate), water n twice and the town sign: the word nswt 'king' is set before nn, out of respect, though it is read second (Budge: Sutenḥenen). The seated figure is taken as a classifier of the king. Heracleopolis, in Middle Egypt, was a city of Osiris and of the ram-god Herishef.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · resting · upon · Maat
sentences.i: Hail to you who rest upon Maat!
sentences.n: Strophe 7; ind ḥr·k in red. ḥtp ḥr mꜣꜥt 'resting upon Maat': ḥtp is the offering table with t and p, the participle or the stative, 'who rests, resting'; ḥr 'upon' is the face with its stroke. mꜣꜥt is the plinth mꜣꜥ with t (no sickle printed), and as classifier a seated goddess with the feather holding an ankh (C10, approximate): truth and right order, and the goddess who embodies them. The god's throne stands on Maat.

sentences.l: you · lord · of-Abydos
sentences.i: You are the lord of Abydos.
sentences.n: ꜣbḏw 'Abydos' is the emblem of Abydos (R17, approximate) with b, the hand d, the curl w and the town sign; the hand d stands for ḏ, as the type often has it (Budge: Àbṭu). Abydos was the holy city of Osiris, where his head was said to be buried.

sentences.l: is-joined(?) · to · limbs · your · the-Sacred-Land
sentences.i: The Sacred Land is joined(?) to your limbs.
sentences.n: ḫnm is the jug ḫnm with m and the papyrus roll (Budge prints 'nem' small): a sḏm·f, 'join, be joined with'. n ḥꜥw·k 'to your limbs': the preposition n and ḥꜥw 'limbs, body', the wick ḥ and U15 for ꜥ with three fleshy curls (F51, approximate) and ·k. tꜣ-ḏsr 'the Sacred Land' is the land sign tꜣ, the arm with a wand ḏsr (D45, approximate), t twice and a low sign with a wavy top (N25, approximate) for the hill country (Budge: Tasertet); the house reading is tꜣ-ḏsr, and the second t is not read. The noun subject stands last, after the phrase with n: Budge takes ḥꜥw·k as the subject ('thy limbs are joined to the netherworld'), but then the n would have to mean 'to' before tꜣ-ḏsr, not before ḥꜥw·k. The order is unusual and the sense is not certain; either way the god's body and the cemetery are one.

sentences.l: you · abomination · his · falsehood
sentences.i: You are he whose abomination is falsehood.
sentences.n: ntk bwt·f grg: ntk 'you (are)' with a whole clause after it, bwt·f grg 'his abomination is falsehood', a sentence with no verb: 'you are one whose abomination is lies'. bwt 'abomination' is the foot b, t and w, with a fish (K1, approximate) and plural strokes as classifiers, and ·f (Budge: betu-f, '[who] hateth'; bwt is also a verb 'abhor', and a sḏm·f bwt·f grg 'he abhors lies' gives his sense). grg 'falsehood' is the jar-stand g and r, a bent stick on a flat base (coded T14, approximate) and the bird of bad things as classifiers, with plural strokes; the second g is not written. What a god abhors he does not touch: Osiris lives on Maat and loathes lies.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · who-is-in-the-midst · of-bark · his · who-brings · Hapy · from · cavern · his
sentences.i: Hail to you who are in the midst of his bark, who brings Hapy from his cavern!
sentences.n: Strophe 8; ind ḥr·k in red. ḥry-ib 'who is in the midst of' is the face ḥr and the heart ib (drawn as a jar with ears, F34), with no strokes. wiꜣ·f 'his bark' is w, the reed, ꜣ and a boat (P1, approximate) as classifier, with ·f: the god is greeted and then spoken of in the third person. in 'who brings' is a sign coded W25 (approximate; Budge: àn) with water n as complement; Budge prints the n as a word of its own, and it is joined to in here. ḥꜥpy 'Hapy', the Inundation, is the wick ḥ, U15 for ꜥ, p and two strokes y, with a dotted oblong over three water lines and the seated god as classifiers. m tpḥt·f 'from his cavern': tpḥt is t, p, the wick ḥ, t and a house-like sign (O1, approximate), with ·f (Budge: tepḥet-f, 'his source'). The Nile flood was thought to rise from caverns beneath the earth.

sentences.l: shines · the-light · upon · corpse · his
sentences.i: The light shines upon his corpse.
sentences.n: wbn šw: the sḏm·f wbn 'shine, rise' (w, b, n and the sun) with the noun subject šw 'light, sunlight', the feather šw with w as complement and the sun as classifier (Budge: śu, 'the light'). ḥr 'upon' is the face with its stroke. ẖꜣt·f 'his corpse' is a fish standing above (coded K4, the sign ẖꜣ, approximate) with t and an oval (Aa2, approximate) as classifier under it, and ·f (Budge: χat-f, 'his body'). The sun shines on Osiris lying in the Duat.

morph.gloss: light, sunlight (noun; written with the feather šw and the sun)

sentences.l: he · who-is-in · Nekhen
sentences.i: He is the one who is in Nekhen.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḫ-n; read nḫn 'Nekhen'. The placenta ḫ and water n are followed by a house-like sign (O1, approximate) and the town sign; the first n of the name is not written, and Budge reads Neχen. imy 'who is in' is Z11 im with m and two strokes. Nekhen (Hierakonpolis) in the far south was an old city of Horus.

morph.gloss: Nekhen, Hierakonpolis, the old city of Horus in Upper Egypt (place name; Budge: Neχen)

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · maker · of-the-gods · king-of-Upper-and-Lower-Egypt · Osiris · true-of-voice · who-founded · the-Two-Lands · in · time · his · beneficent
sentences.i: Hail to you, maker of the gods, king of Upper and Lower Egypt, Osiris, true of voice, who founded the Two Lands in his time, beneficent one!
sentences.n: Strophe 9; ind ḥr·k in red. ir nṯrw 'maker of the gods': the participle ir and nṯrw, the flag three times. nswt-bity 'king of Upper and Lower Egypt' is the sedge nsw with t and the bee bit with t (Budge: suten net); wsir 'Osiris' (the seat ws, the eye ir and the seated god) is written inside a cartouche, like a king's name; the ring is not coded. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice, vindicated' is the plinth over the oar, no sickle printed: Osiris was himself vindicated against Seth before the gods. grg tꜣwy 'who founded the Two Lands': grg is a pick set in a block (the sign grg, U17, approximate) with the papyrus roll, the participle of grg 'found, establish', a word spelled like grg 'lie' (Budge: ḳer, 'master of'); tꜣwy is the land sign written twice. m sp·f 'in his time': sp 'time, occasion' is the bolt and p as complements of the threshing floor sp (O50), with a stroke and ·f. mnḫ 'beneficent, excellent' is the gaming board mn with n, the placenta ḫ, a bell-shaped sign coded as the chisel (U22, approximate) and the roll. Osiris is remembered as the king who ruled Egypt before he died.

morph.gloss: to found, establish (verb; a second word of the same spelling as grg 'lie'; Budge: ḳer)

sentences.l: he · it-is · lord · of-the-Two-Banks
sentences.i: It is he, the lord of the Two Banks.
sentences.n: ntf pw nb idbwy: ntf 'he' and pw, the word that marks a sentence with no verb, 'it is he, the lord of …'. idbwy 'the Two Banks', Egypt on either side of the river, is written with two circles, each with a small notch inside (no exact code; coded N9 as a placeholder), and two signs like the tongue of land (N21, approximate): no sign spells the sounds, and the reading follows Budge's àṭeb with the dual of the classifiers. It is doubtful.

sentences.l: may-give · you · to-me · a-way · may-pass · I · in · peace
sentences.i: May you give me a way, that I may pass in peace.
sentences.n: The tenth strophe has no greeting: Ani speaks for himself. di·k n·i 'may you give to me': the giving arm with a loaf (D37) is di, the sḏm·f of rdi used for a wish, with ·k; Budge prints ṭā-k-nà as one group, and it is split here into di·k and n·i, the preposition n 'to' with the seated man ·i. wꜣt 'a way' is the road with shrubs (N31, approximate) with t and a stroke. swꜣ·i 'that I may pass' is the crossed sticks swꜣ with the walking legs and ·i, the sḏm·f again; Budge reads seś-à, another value of the crossed sticks; swꜣ 'pass' is the house reading of this spelling (Spell 125). m ḥtp 'in peace': the offering table with t and p.

sentences.l: I · upright(?) · not · spoke · I · lies · with · knowledge · my · not · did · I · a-deed · second
sentences.i: I am upright(?): I have not spoken lies knowingly, nor have I done a deed a second time(?).
sentences.n: ink 'I (am)' is the pot nw, the basket k and the seated man (no water n printed): the independent pronoun with a word after it. ꜥqꜣ 'upright, exact' is read with Budge (āq), but no sign for ꜥ is printed: two upright strokes (Z4A) and a tall narrow sign with a slanting foot taken as Aa28 (approximate); the reading is doubtful. n ḏd·i grg m rḫ·i 'I have not spoken lies with my knowledge': n is the negative arms (D35, approximate), and n with the sḏm·f denies a past act; ḏd·i is the cobra ḏ, the hand d and ·i; grg 'lies' is the jar-stand g, r, the pick grg (U17, approximate), a stroke and the bird of bad things. rḫ·i 'my knowledge' is r, the placenta ḫ, the roll and ·i. n ir·i sp snnw: ir·i is the eye over a stroke, the stroke standing for the suffix ·i, as in šsp·n·i in the hymn to Ra (Budge: àri-à); sp 'deed, time' is the bolt, p and the threshing floor; snnw 'second' is two upright strokes over the pot nw, the ordinal 'second', so this is not the repetition sign sp sn '(Twice.)'. 'I have not done a deed a second time' may mean that Ani did not repeat a fault; Budge takes it as acting 'with a motive second', double dealing. The sense is not certain.

sentences.l: adoration · of-Ra · when · rises · he · in · the-horizon · eastern · of · the-sky · rejoicing · of · those-in-the-following · his
sentences.i: Adoration of Ra when he rises in the eastern horizon of the sky; the rejoicing of those in his following.
sentences.n: Plate 20 begins a new hymn, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes dwꜣw and ḫft wbn·f in red, Ra and the rest of the title in black. dwꜣw 'adoration' is the hand d and a looped cord taken as wꜣ (V4, approximate), ꜣ, the star dwꜣ as classifier, ꜣ again, the chick w, a man raising both arms (approximated) and the roll, as at the opening of the hymn to Osiris in the first part; Budge prints ṭua-ṭuau. rꜥ 'Ra' is r and U15 for ꜥ, with the seated god wearing the sun-disk. ḫft wbn·f 'when he rises': ḫft 'in front of, at the time of' is the placenta ḫ, the viper f and t, and before a verb it means 'when'. ꜣḫt iꜣbtt nt pt 'the eastern horizon of the sky': ꜣḫt is the sun between hills with t and a house-like sign; iꜣbtt 'eastern' is the emblem of the East with b, t twice and the hill-country sign; nt is the genitive in the feminine, agreeing with ꜣḫt; pt 'sky' is p, t and the sky. ḥꜥ n imyw-ḫt·f: Budge prints ḥā en as one group, and it is split here into ḥꜥ 'rejoicing' (the wick ḥ and U15 for ꜥ, with no classifier) and the genitive n; Budge takes ḥꜥ as a verb, 'rejoice those who …', and either reading is possible. imyw-ḫt 'those in the following' is Z11 im, w and a stroke, the sign ḫt (M3) with ḫ and t, the seated god and a stroke, and ·f; Budge's numeral 2 is printed inside the word.

sentences.l: O · Osiris · Ani · in · vindication · says · he
sentences.i: O Osiris Ani, in vindication! He says:
sentences.n: i 'O' is the reed with a man raising his hand to his mouth (A26, approximate), the interjection that calls on someone; it stands oddly before the dead man's own name, and the scribe may have written it by anticipation of the i that opens the speech. Wsir 'the Osiris' is the eye ir over the seat ws, with the seated god; ꜣny 'Ani' is the vulture ꜣ, water n, three small strokes (not read) and two reeds, with the seated man. m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication' (Aa15 m, the plinth and the oar): mꜣꜥ-ḫrw used as a noun. ḏd·f 'he says' is the cobra ḏ, the hand d and ·f, in red.

sentences.l: O · Disk · this · lord · of-rays · who-rises · in · the-horizon · day · every
sentences.i: O you Disk, lord of rays, who rises in the horizon every day,
sentences.n: Ani's speech begins. i 'O' as before. itn 'the Disk' is the reed i, t, water n and the sun-disk: the visible sun. pwy 'this' (p, the chick w and two reeds y) is the demonstrative after its noun, 'O you Disk'. nb stwt 'lord of rays': stwt 'rays' is the pierced skin st (F29, approximate) with t written three times (two stacked and one beside them; one is the ending, the others complements of st), the chick w, the sun shedding rays and a stroke (Budge: satetu). wbn 'who rises' is the participle (Budge's numeral 3 stands inside the word). hrw nb 'every day': hrw is the sun with its stroke, and nb after a noun is 'every'.

sentences.l: may-shine · you · in · the-face · of · the-Osiris · Ani · in · vindication
sentences.i: may you shine on the face of the Osiris Ani, in vindication.
sentences.n: psd·k 'may you shine' is p, the bolt s, the hand d and the sun shedding rays, with ·k: the sḏm·f of psḏ 'shine', used for a wish, the hand d standing for ḏ (Budge: pesṭ-k). m ḥr n 'in the face of': ḥr 'face' is the face with its stroke, then the genitive n. Wsir ꜣny m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw as in line 2.

sentences.l: adores · he · you · at · dawn · makes-content · he · you · at · evening
sentences.i: He adores you at dawn, he contents you at evening.
sentences.n: dwꜣ·f tw 'he adores you' is written in red: the star dwꜣ with ꜣ, a man raising both arms (approximated), the roll and ·f, a sḏm·f, with tw 'you' (t and the chick w), the dependent pronoun as object; the overline over the red words runs on to the start of line 4. dwꜣyt 'dawn, morning' is the star with ꜣ, two reeds y, t and the sun as classifier of time (Budge's numeral 4 stands before it). sḥtp·f tw 'he makes you content': sḥtp, the causative of ḥtp, is the bolt s, the offering table ḥtp with t and p, and the roll, with ·f; Budge renders 'with praise', which no sign writes. mšrw 'evening' is the owl m with an arm joined to it (the ligature; the arm is not read), the hatched rectangle š (N37, approximate), r, the lying lion rw with w, and a sky with a star hanging from it (N2, approximate) as classifier of night. Morning and evening are the two hours of worship.

sentences.l: may-come-forth · the-ba · of · the-Osiris · Ani · true-of-voice · with · you · to · the-sky
sentences.i: May the ba of the Osiris Ani, true of voice, come forth with you to the sky;
sentences.n: pr 'may come forth' is the house pr with r and the walking legs: the sḏm·f of pri with its noun subject after it, used for a wish. bꜣ 'the ba' is the jabiru bꜣ with the small pot (R7) at its foot; a small tick near the bird's head is not coded. Wsir is the low seat ws (Q2, approximate) over the eye, without the god; ꜣny has a man on a chair holding a flail (A51) as classifier. ḥnꜥ·k 'with you' is the wick ḥ, water n and U15 for ꜥ (Budge's numeral 5 stands before it), with ·k. r pt 'to the sky'. The ba of the dead goes up with the sun in the morning.

sentences.l: may-proceed · he · in · the-Mandjet-bark · may-moor · he · in · the-Sektet-bark · may-mingle · he · among · the-Unwearying-Stars · in · the-sky
sentences.i: may he proceed in the Mandjet-bark, may he moor in the Sektet-bark, may he mingle among the Unwearying Stars in the sky.
sentences.n: Three wishes in the sḏm·f, each with ·f, 'he', the ba. wḏꜣ·f 'may he proceed' is a thin staff with a looped head (coded V24, wḏ, approximate), the chick w and the walking legs; Budge reads utu-f, 'may he go forth'. It is read wḏꜣ 'proceed', as in the same wish in the first part of the spell (wḏꜣ·k, there with the fire-drill ḏꜣ, a similar tall sign); the ꜣ is not written. mꜥnḏt 'the Mandjet-bark', the bark of the morning, is the owl m with the arm ꜥ joined to it, a sign of two crossing curves taken as the netting needle ꜥnḏ (V26, approximate), the hand d, t twice and a boat (P1, approximate); the first part of the spell has the shorter name ꜥḏt with the same sign. mni·f 'may he moor' is the gaming board mn with n, the reed, a mooring post (P11, approximate) and a boat; sktt 'the Sektet-bark', the bark of the evening, is s, k, t twice and a boat. ꜣbḫ·f 'may he mingle' is the emblem of the East (R15, iꜣb) used for its sounds ꜣb, with b as complement, the placenta ḫ, the crossed sticks and a kneeling man carrying a load (A9, approximate) as classifiers, and ·f: ꜣbḫ 'mix, mingle, join with', said of the dead joining the stars; the i of the sign is not read (Budge: àbeχ-f, 'may he go'). iḫmw-wrd 'the Unwearying Stars' is the reed i, ḫ, Aa15 m, the negative arms and plural strokes, then the swallow wr with r, the hand d, a slumped figure (A7, approximate) and the star with plural strokes; Budge's numeral 6 stands inside the word. They are the stars that never cease moving.

sentences.l: the-Osiris · Ani · at-peace · true-of-voice · says · he · extols · he · lord · his · the-lord · of-eternity
sentences.i: The Osiris Ani, at peace and true of voice, says, as he extols his lord, the lord of eternity:
sentences.n: ḥtp·ṯi 'at peace' is the offering table ḥtp alone, with the tethering rope ṯ and the reed i: the stative with the ending ·ṯi, which belongs to the 2nd person and to the 3rd person feminine; said here of Ani, it is either a later use of the ending for the 3rd person masculine or a slip. ḏd·f 'he says' is in red, as in line 2. swꜣš·f 'he extols' is the bolt s, the looped cord wꜣ (V4, approximate), ꜣ, the rectangle š (N37, approximate), a man with raised arms and the roll, with ·f: swꜣš 'praise, extol', a sḏm·f describing what he does as he speaks. nb·f 'his lord' and nb ḥḥ 'the lord of eternity' (Budge's numeral 7 stands between them; he supplies '[saying]').

morph.gloss: the stative ending ·ti (here written ·ṯi), said of Ani, 'he is …': a later use of the ending for the 3rd person masculine, or a slip

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · Horakhty · Khepri · he-is · who-came-into-being · by-himself
sentences.i: Hail to you, Horakhty! He is Khepri, who came into being by himself.
sentences.n: Ani's second speech begins, with ind ḥr·k in red. Budge prints ànet'-ḥrà-k as one group; it is split here into ind and ḥr·k, as in the litany. ind is the reed i, the post nḏ (Aa27, approximate), and the cobra ḏ and the hand d as complements, the word spelled out (Budge: ànet'). ḥr-ꜣḫty 'Horakhty' is spelled out as in the hymn to Osiris: the falcon ḥr, the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ, t, two strokes y and two dotted oblongs (N18, approximate) as classifiers. ḫpri pw 'he is Khepri': ḫpri 'Khepri' is the scarab ḫpr with r, the reed i and the seated god; pw marks a sentence with no verb. ḫpr ḏs·f 'who came into being by himself': ḫpr (scarab and r) is the participle, and ḏs·f 'himself' is the cobra ḏ with the bolt s and ·f under its curve. Khepri, the scarab, is the sun at dawn, the god who made himself.

sentences.l: how-beautiful · rising · your · in · the-horizon
sentences.i: How beautiful is your rising in the horizon!
sentences.n: nfrwy 'how beautiful' is the heart-and-windpipe nfr with f and r as complements, two strokes y and the chick w (Budge: neferiu): the adjective with the admirative ending -wy, 'how beautiful is …', and its subject after it. wbn·k 'your rising' is the infinitive with ·k. ꜣḫt 'the horizon' (Budge's numeral 8 stands before it).

sentences.l: brighten · you · the-Two-Lands · with · rays · your
sentences.i: You brighten the Two Lands with your rays.
sentences.n: sḥḏ·k 'you brighten' is the bolt s, the mace ḥḏ (T3, approximate) with the cobra ḏ as complement, and the sun shedding rays, with ·k: the causative of ḥḏ 'be bright', as in the first part of the spell. tꜣwy 'the Two Lands' is written in two rows, each the land sign with a tongue of land (N21, approximate). stwt·k 'your rays' is st with the curl w, t, the sun shedding rays, a stroke and ·k.

sentences.l: the-gods · all · in · jubilation · see · they · you · as · king · of · the-sky
sentences.i: All the gods are in jubilation when they see you as king of the sky.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes mꜣꜣ·s with plural strokes; read mꜣꜣ·sn 'they see'. nṯrw nbw 'all the gods': the flag three times with the seated god, and nb 'all' with the chick w for the plural. m ḥꜥꜥwy 'in jubilation' is the wick ḥ, U15 written twice for the two ꜥ, the chick w, two strokes and a man with both arms raised, with the roll and a stroke (Budge: ḥāāui): a noun from ḥꜥꜥ 'rejoice', its ending -wy unusual. In mꜣꜣ·sn the eye with the sickle mꜣ below it and two vultures ꜣ is mꜣꜣ 'see'; the bolt s with three strokes is the suffix ·sn with its n left out (Budge: maa-s[en], his brackets). The sḏm·f after a sentence with no verb says when: 'when they see'. tw 'you'. m nswt n pt 'as king of the sky': nswt is the sedge nsw with t, n and a seated long-wigged figure (A40) as classifier (Budge's numeral 9 stands before the m).

sentences.l: the-Lady-of-the-Hour · established · on · head · your · her-southern-one · her-northern-one · on · brow · your
sentences.i: The Lady of the Hour stands firm on your head; her southern and her northern ones are on your brow.
sentences.n: nbt-wnwt 'the Lady of the Hour' is the basket nb with t, then wnwt 'hour', the hare wn with n, the pot nw and t, with a cobra (I12) as classifier: a goddess, here the uraeus serpent on the sun's head. mn·ṯi 'established' is the gaming board mn with n, then a tall hooked sign (coded V13, approximate and doubtful) and the papyrus roll as classifiers, and the ending ·ṯi (the rope ṯ and the reed): the stative of the 3rd person feminine, after its subject. m tp·k 'on your head'. šmꜥt·s 'her southern one' is the tall stem šmꜥ (M26, approximate) crossed at its foot by U15 for ꜥ, t, a tilted oval (coded H8, approximate) and a cobra as classifiers, and the bolt ·s; Budge reads qemāt-s, his old value for the sign. mḥt·s 'her northern one' is the papyrus clump mḥ (M16, approximate) with t, the same two classifiers and ·s. They are the cobra-goddesses of the South and the North, the crowns of the two halves of Egypt, set on the god's brow. wpt·k 'your brow' is the horns wp (F13) with t, a stroke and ·k (Budge: àpt).

morph.gloss: southern (nisba; feminine šmꜥt, 'the southern one', the cobra-goddess or crown of the South)

sentences.l: (iw) · has-made · she · place · her · in · the-front · of-you
sentences.i: She has made her place before you.
sentences.n: iw opens the statement (the reed i and the chick w; Budge's numeral 10 stands before it). ir·n·s 'she has made' is the eye ir, the n of the sḏm·n·f and the bolt ·s, 'she', the Lady of the Hour; Budge prints àri-nes as one group. st·s 'her place' is the seat with t, a house-like sign and ·s, as in strophe 5 of the litany. m ḥꜣt·k 'before you': ḥꜣt 'front' is the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t and a stroke, and ·k.

sentences.l: Thoth · established · in · the-bow · of-bark · your · upon · destroying · enemies · your · all
sentences.i: Thoth stands firm in the bow of your bark, destroying all your enemies.
sentences.n: ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on its standard with t and small strokes. mn 'established, standing fast' is the stative after its subject, as in strophe 4. m ḥꜣt wiꜣ·k 'in the front of your bark': ḥꜣt with wiꜣ 'bark' (w, the reed, ꜣ, a boat on a base with a small cabin, P1 approximate, and a stroke) as a direct genitive. ḥr sswn 'destroying': ḥr 'upon' with the infinitive says what is going on. sswn is the bolt s twice, the hare wn with n, and then a long rounded sign with a tab (coded X4, approximate) over a slab on legs (coded T28, approximate) with three strokes, all doubtful as signs, as classifiers; Budge reads sesunneṭ, and his final ṭ seems to be the same unclear X4-like sign that he reads as ṭ in dgꜣ (line 13), but sswn 'destroy, punish' has no d. ḫftyw·k 'your enemies' is ḫ, the viper f, t, the vulture ꜣ (not read) and a stroke, with ·k; no enemy classifier is printed (Budge's numeral 11 follows). nbw 'all'. Thoth stands at the prow of the sun's bark and fights off its enemies.

sentences.l: those-in · the-Duat · come-forth · in · meeting · you · to · see · image · this · beautiful
sentences.i: Those who are in the Duat come forth to meet you, to see this beautiful image.
sentences.n: imyw dwꜣt 'those in the Duat': imyw is Z11 im with m, w and a stroke, the plural nisba; dwꜣt 'the Duat' is the star, ꜣ, t and a house-like sign. pr 'come forth' is the stative after its subject, ending unwritten. m ḫsfw·k 'in meeting you': ḫsf is the spindle-and-viper ligature (U35, approximate) with the chick w, a man bowing (A16, approximate), the walking legs and plural strokes, and ·k (Budge: χesefu-k); after m it is taken as the infinitive or a noun from it, with ·k as its object, and the w may be the ending of the noun. r mꜣꜣ 'to see': the eye with the sickle and two vultures, and a chick w (Budge: maau) that is not read. sšm 'image, form' is the sign sšm (T32, approximate) with m and a seated long-wigged figure (A40, approximate) as classifier; Budge supplies '[thy]'. pw 'this' after it, and nfr 'beautiful' (heart-and-windpipe with f and r) after the demonstrative. The dead come out of the underworld when the sun passes through it.

sentences.l: have-come · I · to · you
sentences.i: I have come before you;
sentences.n: ii·n·i 'I have come' is written in red: the reed with legs ii, two strokes as complement, the walking legs, then the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i (Budge's numeral 12 stands before it); only one reed is printed. ḫr·k 'to you, before you' is the placenta ḫ and r with ·k: the preposition ḫr, used of coming into a person's presence.

sentences.l: I · with · you · to · see · Disk · your · day · every
sentences.i: I am with you, to see your Disk every day.
sentences.n: iw·i ḥnꜥ·k 'I am with you': iw with the suffix ·i and a preposition makes a sentence with no verb (Budge renders 'may I be'). ḥnꜥ·k is ḥ, n and U15 for ꜥ with ·k. r mꜣꜣ 'to see': the eye with the sickle and two vultures. itn·k 'your Disk' and hrw nb 'every day'.

sentences.l: not · has-been-shut-in · (I) · not · has-been-turned-back · (I)
sentences.i: (I) have not been shut in, (I) have not been turned back.
sentences.n: Two passives in the sḏm·tw·f, each negated by n (the negative arms D35, approximate, with water n as complement), with no subject written, Ani understood: '(I) have not been shut in, (I) have not been turned back' (n with the sḏm·f, here in its passive, denies a past act, as in the last strophe of the litany); Budge supplies '[I]' and renders as a wish, 'may [I] not be'. ḫni·tw is the placenta ḫ, water n, the reed, a face in profile (D19) and U15 as classifiers, and the tw (t and w) of the passive: the verb ḫnr 'restrain, shut in', written without its r as elsewhere in the papyrus (Budge: χenà-tu). šnꜥ·tw is the cord šn (V7, approximate) with n, U15 for ꜥ, a lying lion (E23, approximate; it may be the forearm D40) and the walking legs, and tw: šnꜥ 'turn back, repel'; the lion rw is written in this verb in Spell 1 as well and is not read (Budge: śenār-tu). Budge's numeral 13 stands between the two clauses.

sentences.l: are-renewed · limbs · my · in · seeing · beauty · your · like · favoured-ones · your · all
sentences.i: My limbs are renewed at the sight of your beauty, like all your favoured ones,
sentences.n: mꜣw 'are renewed' is the sickle mꜣ with ꜣ, two small strokes, the chick w and the papyrus roll (Budge: maiu): the sḏm·f of mꜣwi 'be new, be renewed', with its subject ḥꜥw·i 'my limbs' (ḥ, U15 for ꜥ, a fleshy curl, F51 approximate, plural strokes and ·i). m dgꜣ nfrw·k 'in the seeing of your beauty': dgꜣ 'see, look at' is a long rounded sign (coded X4, approximate) over a stand (coded Q7, approximate), ꜣ and the eye as classifier; the two upper signs are read d and g, and the shapes are not certain: the long sign is coded X4 as in dgg 'look' in the introduction to Spell 18, and the stand coded Q7 has no value g, which belongs to the jar-stand W11 it may be. Budge prints ṭeka with an undotted k (his k is k), but dgi 'look at', spelled here with ꜣ, is the word the eye classifier calls for. nfrw·k 'your beauty' is nfr with a stroke and plural strokes, the abstract plural, and ·k. mi ḥsyw·k nbw 'like all your favoured ones': mi is the milk-jug in its net (W19, approximate) with the reed; ḥsyw is the wick ḥ, a tall jar ḥs (W14, approximate), the bolt s, two reeds y and a man with his hand at his face, the plural of the passive participle 'favoured', with ·k; nbw 'all' (Budge's numeral 14 follows).

sentences.l: because · I · one · of · these · of · whom-have-honoured · you · upon · earth
sentences.i: for I am one of those whom you honoured on earth.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes a sun-disk before the genitive n; read n. ḥr ntt 'because': the preposition ḥr with ntt 'that', the conjunction made from the relative nty, introducing a clause; Budge glosses the pair together. ink wꜥ m 'I am one of'. nn 'these, those' is water n, the adze nw (U19, approximate), the pot nw and w (Budge: ennu): the demonstrative before its noun, joined to it by the genitive n. The genitive n after it is printed with a small ring with a dot (the sun-disk N5) before the water-line; the ring has no sense here, and Budge too reads only en. šps·n·k 'whom you have honoured' is a noble seated on a chair (A51, approximate), the bolt s twice, the roll, a stroke, water n and ·k (Budge: śepses-nek): taken as the relative sḏm·n·f of šps 'be noble', used of making someone noble, honouring him; only one s is read, and the verb in this use is not certain. tp tꜣ 'upon earth': tp, the head, as a preposition, and the land sign tꜣ. The favoured of the god on earth are those he favours in death.

morph.gloss: to be noble; with an object, to make noble, honour (?) (verb, from šps 'noble')

sentences.l: (iw) · have-reached · I · to · the-land · of · eternity · have-joined · (I) · to · the-land · of · everlastingness
sentences.i: I have reached the land of eternity, I have joined the land of everlastingness.
sentences.n: iw opens the statement. pḥ·n·i 'I have reached' is the hindquarters of a lion pḥ (F22, approximate) with the walking legs, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i (Budge prints peḥ-nà as one group and renders 'may I arrive'). r tꜣ n ḥḥ 'to the land of eternity': ḥḥ again without its first n. ḫnm·n is the jug ḫnm with m, the roll and the n of the sḏm·n·f; no ·i is printed after it (Budge: χnem-nà, '[may I] be united'), and the 'I' is understood from the clause before. Budge's numeral 15 is printed inside the word, between the roll and the n. r tꜣ n ḏt 'to the land of everlastingness': ḏt is the cobra curling round t over the land sign with grains (N16, approximate). The two lands are one: the realm of time without end.

sentences.l: you · indeed · who-ordained · to-me · it · lord · my
sentences.i: It is you, indeed, who ordained it for me, my lord.
sentences.n: ntk is wḏ n·i st: ntk 'you' with a participle after it, 'it is you who …', strengthened by is 'indeed' (the reed and the folded cloth s, drawn upright). wḏ 'who ordained' is the staff with a coiled top wḏ (V24, approximate) with w as complement and the roll: the participle of wḏ 'command, decree'. Budge prints utu-nà as one group; it is split here into wḏ and n·i 'for me' (water n and the seated man). st 'it' is the dependent pronoun (the bolt s and t), the object. nb·i 'my lord' is the basket nb with a seated long-wigged figure as classifier and ·i. The hymn goes on in the next part with 'O Osiris Ani …'.
